devices.name: Logix Aurelia 16 KB RAM expansion card
devices.description: Optional 16 KB RAM card occupying one Plug and Execute expansion slot. On Aurelia it increases installed RAM from 48 KB to 64 KB. The mapper exposes its four 4 KB pages at B000–EFFF in the normal application view; ROM and video RAM can temporarily overlay those pages without erasing their contents.

memory_mapping.configuration: Firmware discovers the card at startup and maps its pages; no manual address switches.
memory_mapping.system_workspace: The existing 4 KB common system RAM remains at F000–FFFF; the card adds 16 KB to lower RAM.
memory_mapping.service_calls: The common-memory runtime saves the RAM mapping, selects ROM/video RAM for a service and restores the card pages before returning.
memory_mapping.installation: Install with power off, then restart so firmware can discover and test the card.
memory_mapping.application_memory: Lower RAM rises from 44 KB to 60 KB, before other system and workspace reservations.

physical_population.refresh_owner: Host memory controller must refresh the card even while its pages are overlaid; exact interface pending.

manufacturing_requirements: Add eight 16K×1 DRAMs, power/refresh strategy, identification ROM or defined equivalent, page/address decode, buffers, connector, PCB, decoupling and memory-test route. Specify who supplies refresh while the card is hidden by ROM/video RAM.

adapter_requirements.buffer_policy: Local adapter RAM, additional to host system RAM. Partition transmit/receive buffers and metadata; freeze maximum frame length and IP MTU to fit complete frames before implementation. Physical RAM chip count remains unresolved.
adapter_requirements.flow_control: Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Broadcast requires credit from all intended admitted receivers. Timeouts revoke stale credits; bounded queues and retry/error reporting prevent indefinite blocking. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.
adapter_requirements.host_service: No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.

dated_revisions.name: COMDEX 1982 professional graphics revision
dated_revisions.status: Accepted offering specification; production and driver acceptance required before shipment. June specifications and cost snapshot remain the earlier baseline.
dated_revisions.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
dated_revisions.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
dated_revisions.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
dated_revisions.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
dated_revisions.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.
dated_revisions.cost_boundary: November revision assessed separately in comdex_1982_cost_review.json. June cost rows unchanged; quotes and production qualification pending.
